transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... honestly, I just can't seem to keep my work in order anymore. I work at a dry cleaner's, and it's just getting to be too much. The tickets, the receipts, notes from the workshop, customer jobs—it all just gets piled together until I have absolutely no idea what to handle first. It's a mess. 

And you know, speaking of messes, my sister came over last weekend and she brought her new dog, a little terrier mix, and it just tore through my living room. I mean, pillows everywhere, knocked over a plant... I spent the whole Sunday just trying to get the dirt out of the rug. Have you ever tried to get potting soil out of a shag rug? It's impossible. I tried everything, even that foaming cleaner they show on TV, but it just made it worse. Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, work. Yeah, it's just... everything is just in piles at work and I don't know where to start.
When you were a child, did you already have a lot of trouble staying organized or keeping your attention on things?

Oh, yeah, definitely. I mean, even in grade school, my teachers would always tell my mother that I was bright but just... scattered. I was always talking out of turn, losing my papers, needing constant reminders to finish my work. It was like I couldn't keep track of a single piece of paper to save my life. 

Actually, speaking of losing things, just yesterday I lost my favorite pair of reading glasses. I swear I put them on the kitchen counter right next to the toaster, but when I went to look for them, they were just gone. I looked everywhere—under the couch, in the bathroom, even in the refrigerator! Can you believe that? I actually checked the fridge. I mean, sometimes I put the milk in the pantry, so I guess it’s not that crazy. But anyway, my neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she has this theory that there are these little house gremlins that just take your things and hide them for fun. She’s a character, Mrs. Higgins. She makes these amazing snickerdoodle cookies, though. She brought some over last week when she came to complain about the mail carrier. He always leaves her packages on the bottom step instead of the porch... but wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, school. Yeah, my teachers were always having to remind me to just stay on track and finish what I was doing.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or unusually irritable for days at a time?

Unusually high or energetic? No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm always pretty energetic, but not like... not like a crazy amount for days on end. I just have my regular energy, which sometimes feels like too much for other people, I guess. 

Like my boss, Mr. Thompson. He's always telling me to slow down and take a breath. He's this older guy, must be in his seventies, and he moves at a snail's pace. I don't know how he ever gets anything done. And he has this weird habit of chewing on the ends of his pens. Every single pen at the front counter has these little teeth marks on them. It drives me crazy! I tried bringing in my own pens, those nice gel ones? But they smear if you write on the dry cleaning tags, so that didn't work out. I ended up giving them to my niece for her birthday. She loves drawing, especially horses. She drew this one picture of a horse jumping over a fence, and it was so good we actually framed it and put it in the hallway. But anyway... no, I haven't ever had days where I felt unusually high or anything like that. Just my normal, scattered self.
Do you spend a lot of your day worrying?

Worrying? No, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I spend my day worrying. I just get overwhelmed with the piles, you know? But I don't sit around chewing my nails about what's going to happen tomorrow. 

Actually, speaking of chewing nails, my sister used to do that when we were kids. She’d chew them right down to the quick. My mom tried everything to get her to stop. She even bought this special clear nail polish that tasted like hot peppers. It smelled awful, like... like old vinegar and jalapeños. I accidentally got some on my fingers once when I was helping her paint her nails, and I rubbed my eye later that day. Oh my gosh, it burned so bad! We had to flush my eye out in the kitchen sink for like ten minutes. And the worst part was, the water pressure in that old house was terrible. It was just a little trickle. My dad was always saying he was going to fix the pipes, but he spent all his time working on that old Chevy in the garage. He loved that car. It was this bright cherry red... wait, what was the question? Oh, worrying. No, I don't really worry much. Just... distracted, I guess.
Did these concentration and organization problems start only after a head injury, stroke, seizure, or another medical illness?

No, nothing like that. I've never had a head injury or a stroke or anything serious like that. I've always just been this way, you know? Ever since I was a little girl. 

Well, I did hit my head once when I was about seven, but that was just from falling off my bike. It was one of those old Schwinns with the banana seat? Mine was sparkly purple with silver tassels on the handlebars. I loved that bike. I used to ride it all the way down to the corner store to buy those little wax bottles filled with colored sugar water. Do they even make those anymore? They were so good, but the wax would get stuck in your teeth for hours. My dentist, Dr. Miller, he always told me I was going to rot my teeth out. He had this enormous fish tank in his waiting room, filled with all these exotic tropical fish. There was this one angelfish that would just stare at you while you waited. It was kind of creepy, honestly, like it knew you were about to get a cavity filled. I hated getting cavities filled. The sound of that drill... ugh. But anyway, what were you asking? Oh, right, medical stuff. No, no strokes or seizures or anything. Just the normal bumps and scrapes.
